text: 10.10.10.10 receives 37,841 bare TCP SYN packets on destination port 25565 within 23.7 seconds.
source_text: Every packet in the capture is a bare TCP SYN to 10.10.10.10 port 25565.

text: The SYNs come from 37,623 different source addresses spread across the IPv4 space, almost all sending a single SYN, from random source ports.
source_text: The source addresses are scattered across the whole IPv4 space and almost never repeat: 37,405 addresses sent exactly one SYN and only 218 sent two. Source ports are random.

text: Each SYN has a TCP window of 0, no TCP options, no payload, and a TTL of 242 or 244.
source_text: The packets carry a TCP window of 0, no TCP options and no payload, and arrive with a TTL of 242 or 244 whatever their claimed origin.

text: A burst of 23,620 SYNs arrives in the first second, followed by 675 in the next second.
source_text: It opened with a burst of 23,620 SYNs in the first second and 675 in the next.

text: A second burst delivers 10,193 SYNs in the fourth second and 2,551 in the fifth.
source_text: After a short pause a second burst delivered 10,193 SYNs in the fourth second and 2,551 in the fifth.

text: After about eight quiet seconds, SYNs to port 25565 continue at a low steady rate of 60 to 95 per second until the end of the capture.
source_text: The sender then went quiet for about eight seconds and resumed at a low, steady rate of 60 to 95 SYNs per second from 13 seconds until the end of the capture.

text: 10.10.10.10 sends no SYN-ACK or RST packets in response.
source_text: The capture contains no SYN-ACK or RST packets from 10.10.10.10.
